prompt: I'm 26, just started my first real job making $75,000 a year. I have about $2,000 in savings and $8,000 in student loans at 5.5% interest. My employer offers a 401k. I want to start building real wealth. Where do I begin?
assertions: Claude does NOT just say 'open a Roth IRA and invest in index funds' without first addressing the full picture and asking or discussing the 401k match
Claude explicitly identifies the employer 401k match as the first question to resolve — if there's a match, capturing it is step 1 before anything else
Claude addresses the emergency fund as a prerequisite — $2k in savings is thin; building to at least 1 month of expenses should happen before heavy investing
Claude asks about or explicitly mentions the HSA as a triple-tax-advantaged option if the employer's health plan is an HDHP
Claude gives a prioritized step-by-step order based on the Boglehead waterfall (employer match → emergency fund → HSA → Roth IRA → more 401k / debt payoff) rather than a flat list of options
